code:
.text

    .globl main

main:
    la $t0, msg     # t0 = the address of the string

# for each character in the string (strings end with a 0 null terminator!)    
loop:
    # load the character (lb == load byte, similar to load word but 1 byte instead of 4)
    lb $t1, 0($t0)  

    # are we at the end of the string?
    beq $t1, $zero, finished 

    # if not, print the char
    li $v0, 11
    addi $a0, $t1, 0 # set a0 to the current character in t1
    syscall

    addi $t0, $t0, 1 # move to the next character in the string
    j loop           # and continue

finished:
    # exit
    li $v0, 10
    syscall

        .data
msg:    .asciiz "Hello, world!"
description: Load the base address of an .asciiz string into $t0, read one byte at a time with lb, and loop until the 0 null terminator is reached.

steps.description: Declare msg: .asciiz "Hello, world!" in the .data segment on lines 29-30, and load its starting memory address into $t0 with la $t0, msg on line 6.
At loop, use lb $t1, 0($t0) on line 11 to load a single 1-byte character from address $t0 into $t1. Branch to finished with beq $t1, $zero, finished when that byte is the 0 null terminator.

steps.answer: Each ASCII character occupies 1 byte in memory (loaded with lb), so advancing $t0 by 1 byte moves the pointer to the very next character.
steps.question: Why does line 21 add 1 to $t0 (addi $t0, $t0, 1) instead of 4?

steps.description: Print the character in $t1 using syscall 11, increment the pointer $t0 by 1 byte on line 21, jump back to loop, and exit with syscall 10 at finished.
Watch lb $t1, 0($t0) load the first byte ('H', ASCII 72) from the address in $t0.

title: Traversing a Null-Terminated String in MIPS
